chaining: The EUR 175,000 minimum eligible budget is the clause that decides usability: at a 70 percent rate the smallest viable award is EUR 122,500 of subsidy against at least EUR 52,500 of the applicant's own money, so this is a grant for a company already spending, not seed capacity for a person testing an idea.

notes: The 85 percent and EUR 325,000 tier is the number most summaries omit, and it is reachable only by hiring a doctorate holder, which is a real cost rather than a formality. Two readings were considered. (a) The EUR 250,000 cap is per project: refuted, the resolution says 'por entidad beneficiaria', so it is per company across the call. (b) A foreign founder can hold a Spanish S.L. and apply: plausible, because the eligibility test is registration and age, not nationality, and the resolution names no nationality condition anywhere in the articles read. That reading is why the verdict is fails-identity on the company rather than on the person, and it is the cheapest of the company gates alongside Malaysia's RM 1,000 paid-up capital.
